title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken & Potatoes
subtitle: crispy-skinned chicken thighs roasted over baby potatoes in lemon, garlic and dried oregano: one pan, no fuss
imageAlt: Golden roasted chicken thighs and halved baby potatoes on a sheet pan with lemon, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Dried oregano, thyme, paprika, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Oven at 220°C (425°F) with the rack in the upper middle.
Pat the chicken skin very dry so it crisps.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the olive oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, paprika, salt and pepper in a large bowl.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes in the bowl to coat, then lift them onto the sheet, cut side down, leaving the rest of the mixture in the bowl.

steps.title: Chicken
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry, toss it in the remaining mixture and nestle the pieces skin side up between the potatoes. Pour any mixture left in the bowl over the chicken.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast 40–45 minutes, until the skin is crisp and golden, the potatoes are tender and the thickest thigh reads at least 74°C (165°F) near (not touching) the bone.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over the chicken and potatoes.

fixIt.fix: Pat it drier next time, and give it 3–4 minutes under the broiler at the end; watch it closely.
They were crowded or under the chicken. Keep them cut side down in a single layer.
Move the chicken to a plate under foil and roast the potatoes 5–10 minutes more.
Lemons vary. Drizzle a little honey or olive oil over before serving.

saleTip: Bone-in thighs are one of the cheapest cuts at No Frills, often $5.50–6.60/kg in family packs.
leftovers: Pull the meat off the bone for wraps or a chicken salad sandwich; fry the potatoes for breakfast.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the thickest thigh, not touching the bone (Health Canada, poultry pieces). Thighs are even more tender at 80–85°C.
source: Based on tested sheet-pan chicken thigh methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): bone-in thighs roasted at 220°C (425°F) with potatoes in a lemon-garlic-oregano oil.
prepAhead: Mix the oil and toss the chicken in it up to 8 hours ahead; keep covered in the fridge. Toss the potatoes just before roasting.
reheat: At 200°C (400°F) 12–15 minutes, or in the air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 6–8 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Lemon, garlic, dried oregano, salt and pepper; no dried thyme or paprika.

stepNotes.1: Basic: leave out the dried thyme and paprika.

fancy.note: Roasted lemon slices and a honey glaze on the skin.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: tuck the lemon slices between the pieces.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: brush the honey over the skin for the last 5 minutes.

plating: Serve on the warm sheet pan at the table.

why.0-1: Zest carries the lemon flavour; the juice adds brightness. Using both makes it taste really lemony.
why.1-0: Cut side down on the hot pan, the potatoes brown in the chicken drippings.

funFact: Bone-in chicken thighs are almost impossible to dry out: their fat and connective tissue keep them juicy even past 80°C.

keeps.note: freeze the chicken; the potatoes go mealy
